weightedAverage: 4.53 / 5 (interactionQuality and motionChoreography excluded - not exercised by a static frame)

patterns.flow: pass - input -> per-head projection -> concatenate -> project -> output is a legible staged pipeline
patterns.routing: MISMATCH, not scored as pass or fail - routing tests a choice among alternatives where the path not taken stays legible (gating, dispatch, branching). Multi-head attention has no such choice: every head always runs, none is skipped or preferred. The pattern declaration in this case's target.json does not match what the mechanism actually does. Recorded as a target.json authoring mismatch, not a vocabulary gap or a scene failure.

failures.description: Z0/Z1/Z7 use role 'observed' with no identity and no values, which resolves to the RESTING step of ROLE_FILL.observed's 'solid' band - a bold, dark, hue-less fill (no identity to warm it up, unlike case02's Q/K/V output vectors, which used the same solid-observed treatment but WITH an identity hue, and read well). The result reads as a stark near-black square with no number - correct per the role system's own convention (observed = measured data, drawn boldly) but visually more like a void than 'this holds this head's real output' to an unfamiliar viewer.
failures.note: Not filed as a system defect - this is a predictable consequence of choosing role=observed with neither identity nor a value on a scene where head identity is deliberately NOT colour-coded (see below). An authoring choice, and a defensible one, just cosmetically stark.

designValidation: This case could plausibly have needed more than 3 identity slots (8 heads), which would have been a real gap (IDENTITY_SLOTS has exactly 3). It did not: head identity is conveyed through LAYOUT (position, 'head N' labels) rather than colour, and IDENTITY is reserved for its actual purpose within one head - distinguishing Q, K and V as peers of the same role. Recorded because it is a positive validation of the four-axis model, not because anything needed fixing: colour-coding 8 peers was never attempted, so the 3-slot ceiling was never tested here. A case that truly needed 8 colour-distinct peers (not this one) would be the one that finds this gap for real.
